text:
laura-gomez: Hi team :wave: Im planning to be in Mexico City from 2026-09-01 to 2027-02-01 (about 5 months) to care for a family member. I want to stay on Redwood payroll and keep benefits. Is this allowed? Do I need to change homebase or will we need local payroll? Any advice re: WFH stipend and health coverage while abroad?

people-ops: Thanks for flagging this, Laura. Because this is >90 days and under 183 days, Mexico rules may still create employer obligations. We treat anything >90 days as a medium-risk cross-border remote request. Please file the Temporary Remote Work (Cross-Border) form and include exact street address + expected local work hours.

laura-gomez: Filed the form (attached). My manager already approved in DM.

ivan-legal: Quick legal note: Mexico can trigger social security/employer registration depending on the facts (work performed in-country, reporting lines, payroll staying outside MX). Also watch for potential local employment law exposure if youre effectively working from an MX location for months. Well review the form and may recommend local counsel.

laura-gomez: Understood. If Redwood needs to set up local payroll, what happens to my US benefits?

benefits-team: Typically, if you remain on Redwood US legal payroll we try to keep US medical and other benefits intact for short-term. If legal/payroll moves to a local entity (Mexico), medical coverage may change or be supplemented by local plans. Well confirm specifics once payroll/legal decide. If theres a gap risk we can set up short-term travel/expat insurance; ping us and well send options.

dave-payroll: From payrolls POV: inputs we need from the form: exact dates, address, whether youll invoice any local clients (no), and confirmation you wont be engaging as a contractor for Mexican entities. If payroll can remain in the US, well still check withholding obligations. If we need to switch you to a local payroll provider (PEO) well detail pay cadence and tax withholdings and any gross-up. Expect initial triage 3 business days after form.

laura-gomez: Will the WFH stipend continue? Im usually on the US monthly allowance.

people-ops: Stipend policy highlights:
- If homebase stays US and payroll remains US, stipend usually continues but may be prorated month boundaries.
- If payroll or legal employment moves to MX, stipend may be handled by local payroll or converted to a cost-of-living adjustment. Well confirm on the triage.

it-ops: IT note: If you plan to work from Mexico, enable VPN and 2FA before travel. If you need hardware shipped or local power adapters, open an IT ticket ASAP. Shipping internationally may require customs forms and ~2 week lead time.

laura-gomez: Any visa/immigration risk for US passport holders staying 5 months?

ivan-legal: Mexico permits tourist entries for US citizens up to 180 days typically, but immigration officers have discretion. 5 months (~150 days) is within many tourist allowances but confirm passport validity and consult immigration resources. Also, long physical presence increases tax residency risk in some countries; Mexicos tax residency rules consider center of vital interests and >183-day physical presence is a common bright line. Youre under that here, but well verify.

people-ops: Note from policy: anything >90 days triggers a more thorough review. Anything approaching 183 days is high risk and may require conversion to local payroll or additional paperwork.

laura-gomez: If local payroll is required, will I have to pay Mexican social security (IMSS) and will Redwood cover employer contributions?

dave-payroll: If converted to a local payroll provider, local mandatory contributions typically apply. Our approach: we try to avoid surprise net pay changes; for short-term conversions we often do a gross-up or partial compensation adjustment, but specifics vary by country and provider. Well include options in the triage results.

tax-ops-bot: Automated: Please attach a short daily schedule with local timezone hours (e.g., 0900-1700 CST) and confirm if you will meet with local vendors/clients. This helps the tax team assess PE risk.

laura-gomez: Schedule attached. No local clients, internal meetings only.

ivan-legal: Thanks. Well also check whether your presence could create a permanent establishment for Redwood (unlikely for one employee without contract negotiations) but we need to be cautious.

people-ops: Logistics note: housing stipends are not automatic for temporary caregiving moves. If you need relocation support (one-time shipping, short-term housing) submit a People Ops relocation request. For equipment shipping: IT handles outbound shipping but customs fees may fall to the employee unless pre-approved.

benefits-team: For medical: we advise getting short-term international medical insurance if youll be outside US for extended periods. We can recommend a vendor and Redwood can cover the premium in specific hardship cases; will discuss if needed.

laura-gomez: Thanks. Timeline?

people-ops: Plan: 1) Triage within 3 business days after form (payroll + legal). 2) If local counsel needed, well notify you and estimate 5-7 business days. 3) Final decision (payroll/benefits/stipend treatment) within 10 business days unless legal counsel needed.

laura-gomez: Great, appreciate the quick answers. Ill wait for the triage and keep my manager looped.

people-ops: Thanks Laura  well follow up in this thread. If anyone in the company has recent Mexico experience (housing tips, local sim cards), DM Laura. :mexico:
